correctness.rationale: The proof fixes all integer quantifiers and extracts probabilities from a degree-generating weighted spanning-tree polynomial. A Kirchhoff unit-current construction proves the effective resistance (1/x1+1/x2)/Y, and the rank-one matrix-tree update gives Z1=P X^(b-1) Y^(a-2)(Y+x1+x2). Degree-one coefficients yield the stated expectation difference. Strict monotonicity in b and comparisons at b=a-1,a prove the exact sign for all a>=3; a=2 and b=1 are handled explicitly. A pure-Python exact-arithmetic checker passed 14416 assertions, including Kirchhoff cofactor identities, exhaustive small labeled tree enumerations and rational sign tests. The infinite claim rests on algebraic proof, not on finite tests.

value.rationale: The natural structural question is whether adding a previously missing edge to a highly symmetric connected graph increases or decreases mean UST leaves. The exact formula establishes both signs infinitely often and identifies the unique, dimension-free balance threshold for every integer a>=2,b>=1, with a single equality exception. This is a motivated complete classification of a stochastic structural sensitivity, not an arbitrary finite slice or an unquantified counterexample.
